That sounds nice, but I have a lot of problems with this quote.

  1. Only a foolish man thinks he is wise, or that there is such a thing as a 'wise man'. Wisdom in one or many things does not make one wise in all things, or wise in general.

  2. While you may not be able to* teach* someone wisdom in the conventional sense, you can help guide them on their journey. Saying that you can't leads to and justifies inaction.

Some can argue that wisdom itself is purely, experience. Experience cannot be taught. It has to, by necessity, be experienced.

Edit: Furthermore, as the quote states, "Knowledge can be communicated, but not wisdom..." This eludes to the fact that most knowledge is done through second hand observation. Wisdom itself is derived through first-hand experience, hence, wisdom cannot be taught, and may, indeed, sound foolish to those who have never had the experiences.
